title: Support Fish Speech on CUDA in worker image and verify on AWS Batch
description: Implement Fish Speech Linux/CUDA synthesis in worker-image using fish-speech with PyTorch/CUDA, pre-bake requirements into Dockerfile, deploy worker image, and verify audio generation on AWS Batch GPU queue.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Resolved CUDA OOM and DAC vocoder dtype mismatch; reference audio encoded and text tokenized. Diagnosed upstream generate_long constraint (max_length - 2048 prompt limit), increased max_length to 8192, and triggered workflow build 35286091666.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Diagnosed OOM during DAC vocoder decoding: max_length=8192 allocated 1.3GB of KV caches, exhausting the 16GB T4 GPU right before DAC snake activation. Decreased max_length to 4096 (which still leaves 2048 prompt capacity vs 178 needed) saving 675MB VRAM, enabled PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, and added explicit CUDA cache flushing. Dispatched worker image build 35340491402.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Offloaded Fish Speech DAC vocoder to CPU to eliminate CUDA VRAM contention with 3.6B LLaMA model on 16GB GPU. Added recursive tensor device transfer in _safe_encode and worker request loop so prompt embeddings flow seamlessly from CPU encoder to CUDA LLaMA. Dispatched build 35350265313.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Resolved CUDA/CPU device mismatch by overriding kwargs['device']=device in _launch_thread_safe_queue and adding _safe_forward_generate wrapper. Verified on AWS Batch GPU job f3e2d598: synthesized all 3 blocks with 9.84 GB GPU peak memory, decoded audio on CPU, uploaded 7.1 MB WAV audio/b3ece5e9.wav to S3, and marked job status as done. All 9 website examples now return HTTP 200/206 audio.
